newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe sinks to new low in opinion poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe sinks to new low in opinion poll.

text.p: The approval rating of French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, under fire for government austerity policies at a time of persistently high unemployment, fell to a new low in an opinion poll made public on Wednesday.

Just 25 percent approved of Juppe's performance in office while 72 percent disapproved in the latest Gallup poll for the weekly L'Express, the least favourable rating since he became prime minister in May 1995.

President Jacques Chirac's approval rating also fell in the new survey, to 35 percent, though it remained above his previous low of 29 percent, recorded a year ago during crippling transport and public sector strikes.
Fifty-six percent of those surveyed disapproved of the president's performance, according to the poll.

With unemployment at a record high 12.6 percent in September, Chirac and Juppe have moved to cut back on state spending and public sector payrolls to help France qualify for a single European currency.
Their austere agenda has contributed to sporadic labour unrest over the past few months.
The poll was based on interviews with 950 individuals of voting age conducted last Thursday and Friday.
